title: Cost Management Alerts

controlTest.positiveScenario: Inject sample events matching UC-4.2.12 SPL; confirm the search returns rows and alert fires.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Replay benign traffic without matching markers; confirm UC-4.2.12 search returns zero rows.

dataSources: `index=azure` sourcetype=`azure:costmanagement` collected via `Splunk_TA_microsoft-cloudservices`, Azure Cost Management export; validate ingest with `| stats count by sourcetype`.
spl:
index=azure sourcetype="azure:costmanagement"
| table _time ResourceId Cost PreTaxCost Currency
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.2.12_cost_management_alerts_12"
| sort -_time
description: Azure cost monitoring prevents budget overruns. Tracking spend by resource group/team enables chargeback and anomaly detection.
value: Detecting cost management alerts early reduces mean time to contain cloud incidents, supports audit logging controls, and prevents silent misconfiguration drift across accounts.
implementation: Configure Azure Cost Management to export daily usage data to a storage account. Ingest in Splunk. Create budget alerts when spending approaches thresholds.
visualization: Stacked area chart (spend by RG), Line chart with budget overlay, Table.
knownFalsePositives: Cloud billing and cost files often arrive a day or more late, include credits and refunds, and use tags that do not line up with app names, so a spike is not always a real overrun. We narrow alerts to sustained trends and we exclude test or sandbox projects when we can.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud with search access to `index=azure`.
• Install and configure `Splunk_TA_microsoft-cloudservices`, Azure Cost Management export with the modular input for `azure:costmanagement`.
• Prerequisite crawl UC(s): UC-4.2.58.
• Confirm field extractions in `props.conf` for `ResourceId` and related actor fields.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Configure Azure Cost Management to export daily usage data to a storage account. Ingest in Splunk. Create budget alerts when spending approaches thresholds.
Validate ingest before alerting:
```spl
index=azure sourcetype="azure:costmanagement" | stats count by sourcetype
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=azure sourcetype="azure:costmanagement"
| table _time ResourceId Cost PreTaxCost Currency
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.2.12_cost_management_alerts_12"
| sort -_time
```

Understanding this SPL
Scopes `azure:costmanagement` in `index=azure` to detect cost management alerts. Tune thresholds to your change cadence; exclude break-glass principals and sandbox accounts via a lookup.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare to the provider cloud console audit view for the same 24-hour window. Confirm row counts and `ResourceId` values match the vendor console. Run `| fieldsummary` on a 1-hour sample to verify extractions.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Save as `4_2_12_alert` with severity aligned to `low` criticality. Dashboard: Stacked area chart (spend by RG), Line chart with budget overlay, Table..
Failure modes: (1) no events — verify modular input/API credentials and index routing; (2) empty actor fields — upgrade `Splunk_TA_microsoft-cloudservices`, Azure Cost Management export and review alias mappings; (3) API throttling — reduce poll frequency or enable queue buffering; (4) alert fatigue — tune thresholds and document exclusions in knownFalsePositives.
grandmaExplanation: We watch cloud logs for signs of cost management alerts so your team catches problems in your online services before customers or auditors do.
